conclusions: The operating claims in the investment thesis are confirmed. The USD 176bn backlog is real, orders grew 88% organically, gas turbine backlog is 116 GW, and demand from data centres and grid replacement is physical rather than narrative.

The valuation claim is not tested by those facts. At approximately 40x FY2026E EBITDA on a business guiding 12-14% margins, GE Vernova is priced as a structural growth compounder rather than a cyclical industrial in an order boom.

The most important finding is in the cash flow. Guided free cash flow of USD 11.5-12.5bn against roughly USD 6.0bn of adjusted EBITDA is roughly twice earnings, which comes from customer advances on an order book growing 88%. Underlying free cash flow is estimated at roughly a third of the guided figure.
Blended fair value is approximately USD 599 against USD 943 — roughly 36% below. This sits far beneath a sell-side consensus of USD 1,236 whose lowest target, USD 940, is the current price.

The reverse valuation makes the bet explicit: the price requires roughly double the current EBITDA at a generous 20x multiple. That is achievable by 2030 if scarcity pricing survives a 50% capacity expansion — which is precisely what the expansion is designed to end.
thesisImpact: The five phases confirm the thesis's operating claims and reject its valuation implication. GE Vernova is an excellent business in an extraordinary cycle, priced as though the cycle is a permanent structural condition. The correct posture is to want to own this at a lower price, and to watch the cash flow statement rather than the order book.

memo.weighting: DCF 40%, EV/EBITDA 35%, sum-of-the-parts 25%. The DCF is built on estimated UNDERLYING free cash flow of roughly USD 4-5bn rather than the guided USD 11.5-12.5bn, because that guidance is substantially customer advances. This single judgement drives the conclusion and is stated openly: a reader who believes the guided figure is sustainable earnings should flex it in the workspace, and will get a very different answer. Confidence in this rating is LOW — lower than for Apple, Alphabet or Mastercard — because the company is two years old as a standalone, has no through-cycle record, and the disclosure that would settle the cash flow question is not available here.

nonConsensus.market: Free cash flow guidance of USD 11.5-12.5bn shows the earnings power of the backlog.
nonConsensus.us: It shows the balance sheet effect of an order book growing 88%. Free cash flow at twice adjusted EBITDA is not operating cash generation in a capital equipment business — it is customer deposits on equipment not yet built. Note that management raised the cash flow guidance by roughly USD 5bn while leaving the EBITDA margin guidance unchanged. That is the tell.
nonConsensus.evidence: Phase 3 and 4: FY2026 guidance of USD 11.5-12.5bn FCF against 12-14% EBITDA margin on USD 45.5-46.5bn of revenue.

nonConsensus.market: The USD 176bn backlog derisks the next decade.
nonConsensus.us: The backlog is a stock that depletes as it converts. At 116 GW against 20 GW of annual output the queue is 5.8 years; at the 2030 target of 30 GW it is under four. The company is deliberately halving the scarcity that justifies its pricing, and Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi are expanding into the same demand.
nonConsensus.evidence: Phase 2: the queue arithmetic against the published capacity schedule.

nonConsensus.market: GE Vernova is the premier infrastructure equity of the electrification cycle.
nonConsensus.us: On franchise, yes. On price, it trades at roughly 40x EBITDA with a consolidated margin of 12-14% and a structurally loss-making Wind segment whose orders fell 40%. The premier franchise and the premier price are different propositions, and the thesis conflates them.
nonConsensus.evidence: Phase 1 and 4: segment margins of 17-20% diluted to 12-14%; Wind orders down 40%.

fears.text: This analysis is 36% below the market and below the lowest of thirty published targets. Thirty analysts rate it a buy and none rate it a sell.
fears.why: When the entire covering universe is on the other side, the base rate favours them. The specific risk is that the electrification cycle is genuinely multi-decade and that a 2028-30 EBITDA of USD 12bn+ makes today's price look cheap in hindsight.

fears.text: The demand driver is physical and enormous. Data centre load growth and grid replacement are not narratives — they are construction projects with financing attached.
fears.why: Unlike most expensive equities, the demand here is visible and contracted. The bear case rests on pricing normalising, not on demand disappointing.

fears.text: Electrification may be a structurally better business than the analysis credits, with transformer and switchgear shortages that outlast the gas turbine cycle by years.
fears.why: It is guided to 18-20% margins on USD 14.5-15.0bn of revenue with far less new supply entering than in turbines.

A competitor announces gas turbine capacity expansion beyond 25 GW annually

memo.reEntry: Blended fair value is approximately USD 599 and the bull case approximately USD 796. A 20% margin of safety implies adding below approximately USD 480, which is far below the 52-week range and therefore not a realistic near-term entry. The more useful test is evidentiary: two consecutive quarters in which free cash flow approximates adjusted EBITDA — demonstrating that the cash is operating rather than advances — would materially change this analysis, as would consolidated margins sustained above 16%.
